issues.description: The problem statement/UML defines a Stock class and specifies a static SealSaloon.stock attribute of type Stock, but the provided code uses an Inventory class for the same responsibility while Stock.java is empty in the template. Specifically: the UML lists class Stock with its API (problem_statement.md lines 49-55) and the text requires a static stock attribute of type Stock (problem_statement.md lines 77-82). The template/solution provide src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java (an implemented inventory class) and SealSaloon in the solution declares the stock field as type Inventory (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java lines 3-6). The template also contains an empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java file. This naming/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory and an empty Stock.java) will confuse students mapping the UML/spec to the code and may lead them to edit or look for functionality in the wrong file.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the concept name consistent across the specification and code. Either: (A) Rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (class Stock in src/.../Stock.java), update all references (SealSaloon.stock type and any imports), and remove or repurpose the empty Stock.java; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and remove the empty Stock.java. Ensure the chosen class file contains the API described in the UML (add/find/addToStockIngredients/take/emptyStock) so students can directly map requirements to the provided code.
